assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED is the architecture that turned superconducting circuits into controllable quantum machines: strong coupling of a single microwave photon to an artificial atom, dispersive qubit readout, and the basis for essentially all modern superconducting processors. The idea is original, clearly defined and has had pervasive lasting impact on quantum technology and on microwave quantum optics.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the foundational theory with collaborators, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling and dispersive readout experimentally. A theory-plus-two-experiments split is a natural, defensible configuration. Credit nearby (e.g. Girvin, Huang, Majer, Devoret) is not in the supplied names, so the three-name set is a compromise rather than a clean partition of credit.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups and industrial platforms over roughly two decades, and the interpretation is entirely stable. Timing is very good, though the 2025 prize recognised circuit macroscopic quantum phenomena, so the committee must judge whether a further superconducting-circuit prize is too soon.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits may make this look like a near-repeat of the field.
Several important contributors lie outside the supplied credited names.
As a circuit-QED theorist I have a close subject-matter interest, so I cannot claim neutral distance and the claims here come from my own knowledge, not independent verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realisation set the template for quantum computing with controllable qubits, and trapped ions remain a leading high-fidelity platform. Originality and conceptual clarity are high, and the work links directly to the quantum-computing programme.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear theoretical originators; Blatt led the key experimental implementations among the supplied names. Wineland, a central experimentalist, was already recognised in 2012 for ion control, which narrows the open credit space but leaves an experimentalist role for Blatt. Other trapped-ion experimentalists (e.g. Monroe) are not available in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation and commercial systems. Timing is arguably late rather than premature. Partial overlap with the 2012 prize is a consideration.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Haroche-Wineland prize may count against it.
Division of experimental credit between Blatt and other ion groups is not fully settled.
Zoller also appears in the optical-lattice entries, creating a possible competing use of the same laureate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with magic-wavelength trapping and the associated frequency-comb and ultrastable-laser technology, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and underpins tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. This is a clear invention with outstanding precision-measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock concept and Ye developed the strontium implementation to record accuracy; both are in the supplied names, giving a clean two-person configuration. Others (Hall and Hansch, already honoured in 2005; Hollberg, Ludlow) are outside this list and I cannot adjudicate their shares.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with many independent clocks worldwide. The redefinition of the second is pending, which suggests timing is good but not yet capstoned.
uncertainties: The relative weight of Katori's concept versus Ye's technical development I judge from general knowledge.
The 2005 Nobel Prize already covered the frequency comb and may be seen as partial overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a major branch of condensed-matter physics, introducing Z2 topology, protected edge states and a template for topological phases with links to Majorana-based quantum computing. The theoretical idea is original and the experimental confirmation is clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological classification and quantum spin Hall effect in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe, following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's prediction. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore are not in the supplied names, so the credit set is incomplete and any selection contested.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed across several materials and many groups. Timing is good; the 2016 prize recognised topological phase transitions, so this would be a related but distinct recognition.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested: Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele and Moore-Balents are not all available.
The 2016 prize overlap on topology is a consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moire quantum materials, with broad conceptual and experimental reach. The work is highly original and has had immense impact in a short time.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discoveries. This is a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, though the first author of the discovery papers and other theorists are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is strong across many labs, but the field is only about eight years old; the deeper theoretical interpretation of the superconductivity remains unsettled, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and some correlated phases are not fully understood.
Some key early contributors, including the first author of the discovery papers, are not in the supplied names.
Prizes for very recent work carry a risk of premature recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold atoms in optical lattices, with the Mott-insulator transition, the Jaksch-Zoller Hubbard-model proposal and quantum-gas microscopy, established quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. The work is conceptually clear and widely influential, though it is a broad programme rather than one discovery.
assessment.attribution: Zoller made the foundational theoretical proposal, Bloch drove the experimental programme and Greiner contributed the Mott-insulator observation and microscopy. Hanns-Christoph Nagerl, Hulet, Jaksch and others are outside the supplied list, so the compound credit is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with independent confirmation and a developing quantum-simulation field. The 2001 prize on Bose-Einstein condensates covers the earlier foundations, and the subsequent programme is now ripe for recognition.
uncertainties: Reuse of Zoller across entries makes the prize configuration competitive with the trapped-ion candidates.
Whether the discovery is a single prize-sized idea or an extended field is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Loss-DiVincenzo proposal for spin qubits in quantum dots and its experimental realisation produced silicon and germanium spin qubits that are compatible with semiconductor manufacturing. The proposal is original and the platform has major long-term promise for scalable quantum computing.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo proposed the scheme and Vandersypen led central experimental demonstrations, such as spin control and two-qubit gates in silicon. Other experimental groups (Tarucha, Kouwenhoven, Petta, Morello, Dzurak) are not in the supplied names, which makes experimental credit uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Substantial independent confirmation, though the platform is still maturing relative to superconducting circuits and ions. Scalability has not been demonstrated at the level of competing platforms.
uncertainties: Experimental credit is spread among many groups not listed here.
Impact on practical large-scale quantum computing is not yet proven.
Recognition could be viewed as premature relative to ions and superconducting circuits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-state cooling and quantum control of mechanical resonators, including quantum states of motion coupled to superconducting qubits and optomechanical cavities, show that macroscopic objects obey quantum mechanics. The experiments are conceptually clear and connect to quantum sensing and transduction.
assessment.attribution: Cleland's group demonstrated mechanical quantum ground-state and single-phonon control with a superconducting qubit, Teufel reached sideband cooling to the ground state in a circuit, and Aspelmeyer led optomechanical quantum control and entanglement. Other leaders (Painter, Schwab, Lehnert, Kippenberg) are outside the supplied names, so credit is difficult to settle fairly.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent groups, but applications are still emerging and the field has not yet had a broad technological effect, so the case is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The compound discovery spans several platforms with disputed credit allocation.
Recognition may be premature compared to ions, circuits and lattices.
My own familiarity with the circuit-based experiments could bias my view.
